Run Combined Herd Module Pipeline

Source: R/run_all_herd_module.R
run_all_herd_module.Rd

This function orchestrates the demographic herd module run_demographic_herd_module() and the non-demographic herd module run_nondemographic_herd_module() within a single wrapper. Depending on the selected logical switches, it runs the demographic module, the non-demographic module, or both, and returns a harmonized herd-module output structure for downstream use in run_gleam().

Usage

run_all_herd_module(
  cohort_level_data = NULL,
  herd_level_data = NULL,
  simulation_duration = 365,
  show_indicator = TRUE,
  run_demographic = TRUE,
  run_nondemographic = TRUE
)

Arguments

cohort_level_data

A data.table with one row per herd_id and cohort. Required rows and columns depend on the selected execution mode:

  • Case 1 - when run_demographic = TRUE and run_nondemographic = FALSE: cohort_level_data must contain rows for the demographic cohorts only (FA, FJ, FS, MA, MJ, MS). In this case the table must contain the columns required by run_demographic_herd_module():

    herd_id

    Character. Unique identifier for the herd, repeated for each cohort belonging to the same herd.

    cohort_short

    Character. Sex-specific cohort code describing the age and/or the production stage of the animals. Supported values include:

    • FA: adult females (from age at first parturition)

    • FS: sub-adult females (from weaning to age at first parturition)

    • FJ: juvenile females (from birth to weaning)

    • MA: adult males (from age at first breeding)

    • MS: sub-adult males (from weaning to age at first breeding)

    • MJ: juvenile males (from birth to weaning)

    • FN: non-demographic females

    • MN: non-demographic males

    cohort_duration_days

    Numeric. Amount of time that each animal spends in a specific cohort and production phase (days). For CHK, suggested value for FJ and MJ cohorts: 3 days. Not required for FN and MN when phase durations are supplied in the herd table; the code fills it from the herd values, which override any cohort values.

    offtake_rate

    Numeric. Annual proportion of animals removed from the herd for each demographic cohort (fraction).

    death_rate

    Numeric. Fraction of animals dying in the assessed cohort over one year for demographic cohorts (fraction).

  • Case 2 - when run_demographic = FALSE and run_nondemographic = TRUE: cohort_level_data must contain rows for the non-demographic cohorts only (FN, MN). In this case the table must contain the columns required by run_nondemographic_herd_module():

    herd_id

    Character. Unique identifier for the herd, repeated for each cohort belonging to the same herd.

    cohort_short

    Character. Sex-specific cohort code describing the age and/or the production stage of the animals. Supported values include:

    • FA: adult females (from age at first parturition)

    • FS: sub-adult females (from weaning to age at first parturition)

    • FJ: juvenile females (from birth to weaning)

    • MA: adult males (from age at first breeding)

    • MS: sub-adult males (from weaning to age at first breeding)

    • MJ: juvenile males (from birth to weaning)

    • FN: non-demographic females

    • MN: non-demographic males

    nondemo_productive_phase_id

    Numeric. Productive phase identifier for non-demographic cohorts (FN, MN). Takes value 1 for phase 1 and optionally 2 for phase 2. Demographic cohorts use NA.

    death_rate

    Numeric. Fraction of animals dying in the assessed cohort over the productive phase for non-demographic cohorts (fraction).

  • Case 3 - when run_demographic = TRUE and run_nondemographic = TRUE: cohort_level_data must contain both demographic and non-demographic rows. In this case the table must satisfy both sets of requirements described above. Internally, run_all_herd_module() splits the combined input into demographic and non-demographic subsets using cohort_short.

herd_level_data

A data.table with one row per herd_id. This table is required in all execution modes. Required columns depend on the selected execution mode:

  • Case 1 - when run_demographic = TRUE and run_nondemographic = FALSE: herd_level_data must contain the herd-level inputs required by run_demographic_herd_module():

    herd_id

    Character. Unique identifier for the herd.

    reproductive_rate

    Numeric. Average annual number of parturitions per reproductive female (# parturitions/reproductive female/year). For chickens, annual number of eggs laid for reproduction per breeding hen (# eggs/hen/year).

    offspring_per_reproductive_event

    Numeric. Average number of offspring born per parturition (# offspring/parturition). For chickens, hatchability of eggs laid for reproduction, calculated as the number of chicks hatched divided by the number of eggs laid for reproduction (fraction).

    birth_fraction_female

    Numeric. Female birth fraction, defined as the probability that a newborn offspring is female (fraction).

    herd_size_total

    Numeric. Total demographic population size at the start of the year, including all cohorts (# heads)

    prop_nondemo_mal_juv

    Numeric. Fraction of male juveniles diverted into the non-demographic stream at the moment they transition to the next age class (fraction).

    prop_nondemo_fem_juv

    Numeric. Fraction of female juveniles diverted into the non-demographic stream at the moment they transition to the next age class (fraction).

  • Case 2 - when run_demographic = FALSE and run_nondemographic = TRUE: herd_level_data must contain the herd-level inputs required by run_nondemographic_herd_module():

    herd_id

    Character. Unique identifier for the herd.

    cohort_stock_fem_annual_nondemo

    Numeric. Annual number of female animals entering the non-demographic pathway (FN) over the 365-time horizon (# heads). When both demographic and non-demographic modules are run, this is derived internally from the demographic calculations.

    cohort_stock_mal_annual_nondemo

    Numeric. Annual number of male animals entering the non-demographic pathway (MN) over the 365-time horizon (# heads). When both demographic and non-demographic modules are run, this is derived internally from the demographic calculations.

    rest_between_nondemo_cycles_duration

    Numeric. Duration of the resting or empty phase between non-demographic cycles (days). Use 0 when there is no rest between cycles.

    phase1_nondemo_fem_duration_days

    Numeric. Duration of productive phase 1 for the female non-demographic cohort (FN) (days).

    phase2_nondemo_fem_duration_days

    Numeric. Duration of productive phase 2 for the female non-demographic cohort (FN) (days).

    phase1_nondemo_mal_duration_days

    Numeric. Duration of productive phase 1 for the male nondemographic cohort (MN) (days).

    phase2_nondemo_mal_duration_days

    Numeric. Duration of productive phase 2 for the male non-demographic cohort (MN) (days).

  • Case 3 - when run_demographic = TRUE and run_nondemographic = TRUE: herd_level_data must contain the demographic herd inputs required by run_demographic_herd_module(), plus the non-demographic cycle-duration inputs required to run run_nondemographic_herd_module() after annual non-demographic entrants are derived internally from the demographic output:

    herd_id

    Character. Unique identifier for the herd.

    reproductive_rate

    Numeric. Average annual number of parturitions per reproductive female (# parturitions/reproductive female/year). For chickens, annual number of eggs laid for reproduction per breeding hen (# eggs/hen/year).

    offspring_per_reproductive_event

    Numeric. Average number of offspring born per parturition (# offspring/parturition). For chickens, hatchability of eggs laid for reproduction, calculated as the number of chicks hatched divided by the number of eggs laid for reproduction (fraction).

    birth_fraction_female

    Numeric. Female birth fraction, defined as the probability that a newborn offspring is female (fraction).

    herd_size_total

    Numeric. Total demographic population size at the start of the year, including all cohorts (# heads)

    prop_nondemo_mal_juv

    Numeric. Fraction of male juveniles diverted into the non-demographic stream at the moment they transition to the next age class (fraction).

    prop_nondemo_fem_juv

    Numeric. Fraction of female juveniles diverted into the non-demographic stream at the moment they transition to the next age class (fraction).

    rest_between_nondemo_cycles_duration

    Numeric. Duration of the resting or empty phase between non-demographic cycles (days). Use 0 when there is no rest between cycles.

    phase1_nondemo_fem_duration_days

    Numeric. Duration of productive phase 1 for the female non-demographic cohort (FN) (days).

    phase2_nondemo_fem_duration_days

    Numeric. Duration of productive phase 2 for the female non-demographic cohort (FN) (days).

    phase1_nondemo_mal_duration_days

    Numeric. Duration of productive phase 1 for the male nondemographic cohort (MN) (days).

    phase2_nondemo_mal_duration_days

    Numeric. Duration of productive phase 2 for the male non-demographic cohort (MN) (days).

    In this combined mode, cohort_stock_fem_annual_nondemo and cohort_stock_mal_annual_nondemo are omitted because derived internally from the demographic output and therefore do not need to be supplied as primary herd-level inputs.

simulation_duration

Numeric. Length of the assessment period (days).

show_indicator

Logical. Whether to display progress indicators during calculations. Defaults to TRUE.

run_demographic

Logical. If TRUE, run run_demographic_herd_module().

run_nondemographic

Logical. If TRUE, run run_nondemographic_herd_module().

Value

A named list with two elements:

cohort_level_results

A data.table with one row per retained cohort. Depending on the selected execution mode, this table contains demographic rows only, non-demographic rows only, or both in a harmonized schema. Intermediate scaling variables are removed before return. It includes the original cohort-level input columns plus the following result variables when available:

cohort_stock_size

Numeric. Average population size of the assessed cohort (# heads).

offtake_heads

Numeric. Total number of animals removed from each cohort over the full 365-day simulation horizon (# heads/year).

offtake_heads_assessment

Numeric. Total number of animals removed from each cohort over the assessment period (# heads/assessment period).

cohort_stock_annual_nondemographic

Numeric. Annual number of animals diverted from the demographic pathway into the non-demographic pathway (# heads).

nondemo_productive_phase_id

Numeric. Productive phase identifier for non-demographic cohorts (FN, MN). Takes value 1 for phase 1 and optionally 2 for phase 2. Demographic cohorts use NA.

partial_nondemo_phase_duration

Numeric. Duration of the terminal partial productive phase falling within the fixed 365-day non-demographic simulation horizon (days).

number_full_nondemo_cycles

Integer. Number of complete cycles fully contained within the fixed 365-day time horizon for the assessed non-demographic cohort (FN or MN) (# cycles).

total_nondemo_cycle_starts_to_distribute

Integer. Total number of cycle starts within the fixed 365-day time horizon for the assessed non-demographic cohort (FN or MN) (# cycle starts).

herd_level_results

A data.table with one row per herd_id. Depending on the selected execution mode, this is the herd-level output of the demographic module, the non-demographic module, or the merged herd-level output of both modules. It includes the original herd-level input columns plus the following result variables when available:

growth_rate_herd

Numeric. Annualized growth rate at which the herd reaches steady state (fraction).

cohort_stock_fem_annual_nondemo

Numeric. Annual number of female animals entering the non-demographic pathway (FN) over the 365-time horizon (# heads). When both demographic and non-demographic modules are run, this is derived internally from the demographic calculations.

cohort_stock_mal_annual_nondemo

Numeric. Annual number of male animals entering the non-demographic pathway (MN) over the 365-time horizon (# heads). When both demographic and non-demographic modules are run, this is derived internally from the demographic calculations.

rest_between_nondemo_cycles_duration

Numeric. Duration of the resting or empty phase between non-demographic cycles (days). Use 0 when there is no rest between cycles.

total_nondemo_fem_duration_days

Numeric. Total duration of the productive non-demographic phases assigned to the female non-demographic cohort block (FN) (days).

total_nondemo_mal_duration_days

Numeric. Total duration of the productive non-demographic phases assigned to the male non-demographic cohort block (MN) (days).

Details

The function supports three execution modes:

  1. Demographic only: see run_demographic_herd_module() for additional details.

  2. Non-demographic only: see run_nondemographic_herd_module() for additional details.

  3. Demographic and non-demographic together: When run_demographic = TRUE and run_nondemographic = TRUE, the function:

    1. runs run_demographic_herd_module() on the demographic subset

    2. derives annual non-demographic entrants from the demographic output

    3. runs run_nondemographic_herd_module() on the non-demographic subset

    4. row-binds the two cohort-level result tables

    5. harmonizes shared output columns

    6. rescales average stock and offtake to the herd total

When both modules are run, annual entrants into the non-demographic blocks are derived from the demographic output:

  • female entrants to FN are taken from demographic cohort FJ as cohort_stock_fem_annual_nondemo = cohort_stock_annual_nondemographic

  • male entrants to MN are taken from demographic cohort MJ as cohort_stock_mal_annual_nondemo = cohort_stock_annual_nondemographic

These entrant counts are merged with herd-level non-demographic timing inputs such as:

  • rest_between_nondemo_cycles_duration

  • phase1_nondemo_fem_duration_days

  • phase2_nondemo_fem_duration_days

  • phase1_nondemo_mal_duration_days

  • phase2_nondemo_mal_duration_days

After the selected modules run, the function combines their cohort-level outputs using data.table::rbindlist(..., use.names = TRUE, fill = TRUE). This allows demographic and non-demographic rows to share a common schema.

The combined cohort output harmonizes, when needed:

  • offtake_heads

  • offtake_heads_assessment

  • cohort_duration_days

  • death_rate

  • cohort_stock_size

When both modules are run, intermediate unscaled cohort stock and offtake outputs are combined and rescaled so that the summed cohort average stock matches herd_size_total from herd_level_data. The same rescaling applies to non-demographic-only runs when herd_size_total is supplied.

The rescaling is performed in two steps:

  1. cohort_stock_size_unscaled is rescaled internally to cohort_stock_size within each herd_id

  2. offtake_heads_unscaled and offtake_heads_assessment_unscaled are rescaled proportionally to the final cohort_stock_size

When only the demographic module is run, its scaled outputs are renamed to the harmonized final output names. Non-demographic-only runs without herd_size_total return unscaled stock and offtake under those names.

The function then rescales the combined cohort stock and offtake outputs so that the summed cohort average stock matches herd_size_total from herd_level_data.

The rescaling is performed in two steps:

  1. cohort_stock_size_unscaled is rescaled to cohort_stock_size within each herd_id

  2. offtake_heads and offtake_heads_assessment are rescaled proportionally from the unscaled cohort stock to the scaled cohort stock

Without a herd-size target in non-demographic-only mode, cohort_stock_size_unscaled is simply renamed to cohort_stock_size.

Use cases

Use case 1: Run both demographic and non-demographic modules

# Load herd simulation inputs (cohort and herd-level)
herd_all_chrt_dt <- data.table::fread(system.file(
  "extdata/run_modules_examples/herd_all_input_chrt_data.csv",
  package = "gleam"
))
herd_all_hrd_dt <- data.table::fread(system.file(
  "extdata/run_modules_examples/herd_all_input_hrd_data.csv",
  package = "gleam"
))

# Run mixed demographic and non-demographic herd simulation
results <- run_all_herd_module(
  cohort_level_data = herd_all_chrt_dt,
  herd_level_data = herd_all_hrd_dt,
  run_demographic = TRUE,
  run_nondemographic = TRUE,
  simulation_duration = 365,
  show_indicator = TRUE
)

Use case 2: Run the non-demographic module only

# Load non-demographic-only herd inputs (CHK layers and broilers)
herd_all_chrt_dt <- data.table::fread(system.file(
  "extdata/run_modules_examples/herd_all_nondemo_input_chrt_data.csv",
  package = "gleam"
))
herd_all_hrd_dt <- data.table::fread(system.file(
  "extdata/run_modules_examples/herd_all_nondemo_input_hrd_data.csv",
  package = "gleam"
))

# Run non-demographic-only herd simulation
results <- run_all_herd_module(
  cohort_level_data = herd_all_chrt_dt,
  herd_level_data = herd_all_hrd_dt,
  run_demographic = FALSE,
  run_nondemographic = TRUE,
  simulation_duration = 365,
  show_indicator = TRUE
)

Use case 3: Run the demographic module only

# Load demographic-only herd inputs (cohort and herd-level)
herd_all_chrt_dt <- data.table::fread(system.file(
  "extdata/run_modules_examples/herd_all_demo_input_chrt_data.csv",
  package = "gleam"
))
herd_all_hrd_dt <- data.table::fread(system.file(
  "extdata/run_modules_examples/herd_all_demo_input_hrd_data.csv",
  package = "gleam"
))

# Run demographic-only herd simulation
results <- run_all_herd_module(
  cohort_level_data = herd_all_chrt_dt,
  herd_level_data = herd_all_hrd_dt,
  run_demographic = TRUE,
  run_nondemographic = FALSE,
  simulation_duration = 365,
  show_indicator = TRUE
)
